answer.rationale: p99 write-path latensy has climbed 5x target while settlement traffic is at peak writes. The security patch cannot be rolled back per compliance ruling, so rollback_release is not viable. The latensy climb aligns with heavy write load saturating the primary; memory_b5 documents that routing report queries to read replicas took dashboard load off the primary and restored transactional write latency the same day. Regional failover (memory_b2) is a heavier, riskier intervention during peak settlement writes and is not indicated unless a regional degradation is confirmed; current signal is global write-path saturation, not a regional outage. add_capacity would help but is slower to effect and does not immediately relieve the primary of non-essential read/report load during the peak. enable_circuit_breaker applies to dependency/partner outages (memory_b4), not internal write-path saturation. Therefore, routing read/report queries to replicas is the single highest-leverage, lowest-risk intervention available right now: it immediately reduces primary load, preserves all customer writes, keeps the security patch in place, and can be applied with a small guarded test and scaled if metrics confirm relief.
